reader_question: What happens after someone applies for SNAP food benefits, and how long can each step take?
grade_line: Documented: the text of 7 CFR 273.2, as in force on November 9, 2026
title: The federal SNAP rule gives a state 30 days from an application to a decision, and 7 days for a household with very little income or cash; these are the rule’s limits, not measured waits.
measure_line: Steps from a SNAP application to a decision, with the longest time the federal rule allows for each, 7 CFR 273.2 as in force November 9, 2026, United States
notes: SNAP, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, helps households buy food. States run it within these federal rules; a state may move faster, and some miss the limits.
The interview may be held by phone, and the rule lets a state waive it in some cases.
alt: Four steps in order, each a box with who acts and the time the rule allows: file an application, taken the same day; an interview; send proof, with at least 10 days to do it; and a decision within 30 days of filing. A branch from filing leads to expedited service, benefits within 7 days, for a household with very little income or cash.

phone_note: On a phone the steps read down the page, and the expedited branch follows the last step, its line running down the right edge from the first step.
